claims.text: At stage-1 the API is split into three projects: DonHang.Api (controllers, DTOs, middleware, Program.cs), DonHang.Domain (entities, OrderService, INotifier, IOrderRepository) and DonHang.Infrastructure (DonHangDbContext, migrations, EfOrderRepository).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: git ls-tree DonHang.Api DonHang.Domain DonHang.Infrastructure; STAGE.md

claims.text: DonHang.Domain.csproj has no ProjectReference and no PackageReference.
DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj references DonHang.Domain and the packages Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design and Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL.
C# code in a project cannot use types from an assembly or package the project does not reference; it fails to compile (e.g. CS0246).
claims.source_hint: C# compiler error CS0246; .NET project references docs

claims.text: OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync (DonHang.Domain) already checks that an order has at least one item.
The orders route is declared in DonHang.Api (OrdersController [Route("api/v1/orders")]); EF Core queries such as FindAsync with Include live in DonHang.Infrastructure (EfOrderRepository).
A layered architecture groups classes by the kind of reason they change for (HTTP, business rules, data), applying SRP at the scale of an application.
claims.source_hint: outline items 1-2; common description of layered architecture

claims.text: Each layer adds a step to read through and a boundary to maintain, so a very small program does not need several layers.
At run time OrderService (DonHang.Domain) calls into data access only through IOrderRepository and INotifier, interfaces declared in DonHang.Domain; the implementations are in DonHang.Infrastructure.
